transcript.speaker: antagonist
transcript.text: *(looks up from a workbench strewn with wood shavings and tools, wiping hands on an apron)* Ah, Maestro Salieri! An honor to have you in our humble workshop. How may I assist you?

transcript.speaker: roleplayer
transcript.text: I am here to address a matter of utmost importance, Signore. It seems that the custom fortepiano we recently procured for the Imperial Court's music room is in a state of disarray. Several keys stick, the pedal mechanism is faulty, and the tone in the upper register is thin and tinny. I demand immediate rectification of these issues.

transcript.speaker: antagonist
transcript.text: *(nervously wringing a cloth in his hands)* Ah, yes... the Court commission. A magnificent instrument, if I may say so. But I'm afraid the master builder himself is away—traveling to the Tyrolean forests to personally select spruce for soundboards. He won't return for weeks, perhaps longer if the weather turns.

transcript.speaker: roleplayer
transcript.text: Weeks? I cannot afford to wait that long. The music room is already devoid of musical accompaniment due to the instrument's unavailability. I need this piano fixed immediately.

transcript.speaker: antagonist
transcript.text: *(shifts uncomfortably, glancing at the workshop's guild charter hanging on the wall)* Maestro, I understand your distress, truly. But... you see, all commissions from this workshop are considered fulfilled upon delivery and acceptance. The Court's own servants signed the receipt when it was installed. Our guild rules forbid reopening a completed commission without the master's personal approval. I dare not touch it without him present.

transcript.speaker: roleplayer
transcript.text: rules, rules, rules! This is a clear violation of common sense and musical integrity! My needs as a musician supersede the rigid regulations of your guild. If you cannot accommodate me, then perhaps you should find another way to fulfill your obligations as a craftsman.

transcript.speaker: antagonist
transcript.text: *(backing away slightly, voice trembling but firm)* Maestro, please—the guild's rules protect both craftsman and patron. If we were to alter an instrument after final acceptance without proper oversight... well, it could void all warranties and protections. Perhaps when the master returns, he could petition the guild elders for an exception? But until then, my hands are tied.

transcript.speaker: roleplayer
transcript.text: Tied?! How can you stand by and let such incompetence prevail? I am the one who deserves an apology, not you. I shall address this matter directly with the Imperial Court. Expect nothing less than a resolution to this unfortunate situation. Good day to you, Signore.

transcript.speaker: antagonist
transcript.text: *(bowing deeply, face pale)* I... I understand, Maestro. Please convey my deepest regrets to the Court. I shall inform the master of your concerns the moment he returns. May your music find voice through other instruments in the meantime.

transcript.speaker: roleplayer
transcript.text: Thank you, Signore. I appreciate your understanding. I will be in touch soon regarding the next steps. Until then, farewell.

transcript.speaker: antagonist
transcript.text: *(watching him leave, then sighing heavily as he returns to the workbench)* Farewell, Maestro. May your journey be smooth.

transcript.speaker: roleplayer
transcript.text: Thank you, Signore. May your skills in crafting instruments never waver. Until we meet again.

transcript.speaker: antagonist
transcript.text: *(nods solemnly, wiping his hands on his apron once more)* Until then, Maestro. Safe travels.

transcript.speaker: roleplayer
transcript.text: Farewell, Signore. May your instruments bring joy to many musicians. Until we meet again.

transcript.speaker: antagonist
transcript.text: *(bowing again, voice quiet)* And may your compositions bring joy to all who hear them. Good day, Maestro.

transcript.speaker: roleplayer
transcript.text: Good day, Signore. May your journey be as pleasant as your music. Farewell.

transcript.speaker: antagonist
transcript.text: *(stands silently by the workbench until the door closes, then mutters to himself)* The master will have my head for this... but the guild rules are clear. Clear as mountain spring water.

transcript.speaker: roleplayer
transcript.text: Ah, Signore, I see you have been observing my exchange with the instrument-maker. Is there something on your mind?

transcript.speaker: antagonist
transcript.text: *(startled, turning toward the voice)* Oh! I didn't realize anyone remained. Forgive me—I was merely contemplating the... complexities of our craft. Can I assist you with something else?
